how: A member calls for helpers to start another green box at new coordinates.
The later invitation identifies a proposer but does not establish who began the original mark or whether others joined.
A moderator postpones lettering because the room lacks conquered space and manpower.
Borrowing lattice expansion preserves both a green-only rule and the end goal of one solid box.
A member reports a green frame being built in the north east while urging work in the bottom left.
Members correct directional mistakes and supply newcomers with a location and expansion coordinates.
A member explains extra placement capacity through three separate accounts rather than an appointed leader.
A reply assents to putting expansion before conquest without asking for anything back.
The room exemplifies the claim's decided-order minority through a vote and claimed temporary leadership alongside informal coordination.
Internal chat routing connects public recruitment with a reported leader whose decisions remain largely outside the supplied record.
statement: Routing a room's own coordination into live chats and returning reports of decisions or leadership

how: Participants rally to defend an existing Box and Core against other colours.
A participant explains apparently wrong colours as temporary cover work and reports having used them personally.
People request protection for a smiley face, forbid greening art and ask invading blues to spare a named memorial.
An Orange Corner representative offers to extend existing peace to the Box without a recorded acceptance in the cited concept.
The peace offer presents the speaker as carrying an Orange Corner proposal to the Box.
Calls for a joint fight and coalition recruitment do not establish delivered pixels or an exchange of help.
A lattice pledge receives explicit acceptance while other speakers recruit greens into combined efforts.
Joining allies can preserve a distinct final design and exclude a neighbouring shade rather than merge goals completely.
People propose moving to quieter ground and later weigh saving their corner against starting elsewhere.
A later call proposes rebuilding the Box at new coordinates without establishing that rebuilding occurred.
Relocation requires correcting mistaken directions and relaying usable coordinates to people requesting a destination.
Scarcity can produce partial relocation while old positions remain advocated, so moving does not require the whole room to stop fighting elsewhere.
A request to spare a smiley face does not establish guest residence under an acknowledged host's rules.
Informal coordination and a claimed chat leader do not show anyone disputing authority to bind placers to an inter-room agreement.
A peace proposal is visible but no linked answer disputes the proposer's authority or an agreement's binding force.
Praise, teaching, sacrifice and repeated green allegiance make colour faith an explicit part of room conduct.
Members extend the colour's rule from canvas work to the subreddit itself by demanding green CSS.
Colour allegiance supplies a criterion for judging whether a neighbouring grid counts as an ally or heresy.
The event-period concepts name colour enemies but cannot establish a quarrel predating the canvas.
Colour opponents and a Hogwarts reference do not establish that a pre-canvas tie named the rival in an attack turn.
A green CSS demand and devotional praise do not establish that an April Fools host prank licensed the canvas claims as fakes.
An internal chat invitation and a CSS demand do not show a posting boundary around canvas discussion.
Sacrificing a morning and reporting a frame do not establish celebration of a completed work in the coded passages.
A participant records blue damage as desecration of sacred green during the event.
After placement ends a member invites others to recreate the Box on a successor canvas without reporting uptake.
The coded post-close invitation concerns another canvas and supplies no contest over a retained or cleaned historical version.
Participants propose taking a corner and converting Hogwarts into Slytherin.
A member proposes inciting blue and red against each other through words while using tiles on green.
Talk can seek conflict between two opponents to divert them rather than address either opponent in a direct bilateral contest.
Attack and art-restraint concepts occupy separate threads and do not establish a refusal replying to a particular attack call.
Alliance acceptance and calls to unite against enemies do not establish the arrow's enacted mutual defence mechanism.
A call and a report of construction are visible but no coded reply attributes that construction to the call.
The rebuilding call does not establish an original starter followed by a distinct recruitment response.
Calls to defend an existing Core and a separate construction report do not establish the proposed building-to-upkeep transition.
Defence and a later peace offer coexist without a passage linking the offer to pressure from those neighbours.
An offered peace and separate art-restraint instructions do not establish restraint caused by a settled border.
Spare accounts and defence are recorded without a statement that upkeep pressure prompted account multiplication.
The construction report does not include a coded linked celebration caused by completion.
A damage report does not establish that prior celebration prompted recording.
The successor-canvas invitation does not say that preserving an event record prompted continuation.
Design preferences and coordinates are visible without a template settling the design discussion.
The coded bare assent answers a tactical proposal rather than a recruitment call, leaving the specified call mechanism untested.
The joint-fight appeal does not establish that strain elicited delivered outside help.
The peace offer does not establish a resulting trade of pixels or protection.
Recruitment language and attack proposals do not establish that the former brought the latter's participants into the canvas.
An attack proposal and a separate peace offer do not establish a deal answering that proposal.
The plan to incite opponents names a tactic but provides no linked attack-to-talk episode establishing the arrow.
Neither the CSS demand nor chat recruitment establishes that a canvas-post flood caused moderators to draw a posting boundary.
